daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Volatility Rankings with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical price data, calculate the 30-day rolling standard deviation of daily returns for each stock using window functions. Rank stocks by volatility within each month using ROW_NUMBER(). Then use a CTE to identify the top 5 most volatile stocks for each calendar month. Expected output: a table with month, stock_code, volatility_rank, rolling_std_dev, and closing_price. Use LAG() to calculate daily percentage returns, then STDDEV() as a window function partitioned by stock and 30-day windows.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Feature Engineering
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data and perform the following: (1) Handle missing values in injury_level and crash_type columns using mode imputation. (2) Create a new feature 'time_of_day' by binning the crash_hour into periods (morning: 6-12, afternoon: 12-17, evening: 17-22, night: 22-6). (3) Standardise suburb names (strip whitespace, convert to title case). (4) Remove duplicate records based on crash_id, date, and location. (5) Export a cleaned CSV with 10 new columns. Expected deliverable: cleaned_nsw_crashes.csv with no null values in critical columns and consistent data types.

daily_quests.title: Australian Wine Production Pipeline: SQL + Python ETL
daily_quests.description: Build a mini data pipeline: (1) Download Australian wine production statistics by region and vintage year. (2) Use Python pandas to load the CSV, clean region names (standardise case/spacing), validate vintage years (must be 1980-2024), and remove rows with null production volumes. (3) Calculate a new column 'production_per_capita' by joining with ABS population data by region (you may mock this if unavailable). (4) Export to a temporary staging table structure via Python. (5) Write SQL queries to: identify the top 3 wine regions by average production over the last 10 years, calculate year-on-year production growth rate using LAG(), and rank vintage years by total national output using ROW_NUMBER(). Expected output: (a) cleaned_wine_data.csv, (b) a SQL script with 3 analytical queries, (c) a summary report showing top regions and growth trends.
daily_quests.dataset: Australian Wine Production Statistics — Wine Australia (wineaustralia.com) + ABS Census 2021 for population context
